question: Should OpenClaw accept `SecretRef` values in Docker sandbox env knowing the resolved values still become container environment variables visible through Docker daemon/container metadata?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but the requested capability intentionally expands a secret-bearing config surface into a Docker metadata exposure boundary that needs maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Accept with explicit docs and tests
options.body: Allow the SecretRef config shape if the PR preserves literal env behavior, resolves before container creation, registers audit/configure targets, and documents Docker metadata exposure.

options.title: Reject Docker env SecretRefs
options.body: Keep sandbox Docker env literal-only and direct users to existing static env interpolation or external orchestration until a safer secret delivery path exists.

options.title: Defer to a narrower API design
options.body: Leave this issue open for a broader sandbox secret-delivery design that avoids Docker environment variables or gates them behind a new explicit policy.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit docs and tests
recommendation.body: Allow the SecretRef config shape if the PR preserves literal env behavior, resolves before container creation, registers audit/configure targets, and documents Docker metadata exposure.

likelyOwner.reason: This person recently landed the adjacent Docker sandbox env behavior and documented the Docker metadata exposure boundary.
